title: Ram Rumble Bee satış rekoru kırdı ve 2027'ye kadar tükendi
summary: Stellantis'in yeni Ram 1500 Rumble Bee modeli, 5,7 litrelik Hemi V8 motoruyla büyük ilgi görerek 24 saat içinde Mart 2027'ye kadar olan üretim kotasını tüketti.
body:
Stellantis tarafından siparişe açılan 2027 Ram Rumble Bee modeli, otomotiv pazarında büyük bir talep dalgasıyla karşılaştı. The Drive ve Carscoops'un aktardığına göre, aracın 2026 takvim yılına ait tahsisatı sadece 90 dakika içinde tamamen tükendi. Yoğun ilgi bununla da kalmadı ve tüm üretim kotası 24 saat gibi kısa bir süre içinde Mart 2027'ye kadar tamamen doldu. Ram CEO'su Matt VanDyke, "Rumble Bee'nin tükenme hızı, müşterilerimizin performans kamyonetlerine duydukları tutkunun ne kadar büyük olduğunu gösteriyor" dedi.

## Teknik özellikler ve versiyonlar

Giriş seviyesi Ram 1500 Rumble Bee, kaputunun altında stop-start veya eTorque sistemleri barındırmayan 5,7 litrelik bir Hemi V8 motor taşıyor. 59.995 dolardan başlayan fiyatla sunulan bu model 395 beygir güç ile 555 Nm tork üretiyor. Sekiz ileri otomatik şanzıman ve aktif dört tekerlekten çekiş sistemiyle donatılan araç, 0'dan 96 kilometre hıza 6,1 saniyede ulaşıyor. Temel modelin ardından önümüzdeki yıl daha üst düzey olan 392 ve SRT versiyonlarının da ürün gamına eklenmesi planlanıyor.

## Müşteri önceliği ve üretim

Stellantis, sipariş yoğunluğu nedeniyle tahsisat kapsamında yapılan müşteri siparişlerinin öncelikli statü alacağını ve araçların sahiplerine en kısa sürede ulaştırılmasının hedeflendiğini belirtti. Henüz toplam üretim hacmi paylaşılmasa da, bu hamle performans kamyonetleri pazarında iddialı bir dönüşe işaret ediyor.

**Neden önemli?** V8 motorlu klasik performans kamyonetlerinin geleceği hakkında soru işaretlerinin olduğu bir dönemde, Ram'in bu hamlesi pazarın V8 motorlara olan talebinin hâlâ çok yüksek olduğunu kanıtladı.

source_texts.title: The V8 Muscle Truck Isn’t Dead—Ram 5.7 Hemi Rumble Bee Sold Out Through March 2027 in 24 Hours: TDS
source_texts.summary: The market has spoken and America clearly wants a V8-powered muscle truck. The post The V8 Muscle Truck Isn’t Dead—Ram 5.7 Hemi Rumble Bee Sold Out Through March 2027 in 24 Hours: TDS appeared first on The Drive .
source_texts.text:
Good morning, and welcome to The Downshift, which is a lap of today’s top stories from around the auto industry and car culture, curated by The Drive‘s editorial team. Each story gets summarized into a sentence or two accompanied by a link to the source for those seeking more information. Senior Editor Adam Ismail is still out on assignment and I’ll be your driver today.
Here’s what firing on Thursday, October 1, 2026 as fall gets underway:
🔊 The latest episode of The Drivecast, The Drive’s weekly podcast, went live yesterday on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and wherever you get your podcasts.
💪 Stellantis opened orders for the 2027 Ram Rumble Bee with the 5.7-liter Hemi V8 and all 2026 models were spoken for in 90 minutes while production through March 2027 was sold within 24 hours. “The speed at which the Rumble Bee sold out speaks volumes about the passion our customers have for performance trucks,” said Matt VanDyke, CEO of Ram. Notably, Ram hasn’t released production volumes and it’s unclear how many Rumble Bees are being made instead of Big Horns or Long Horns, though the margins on a Rumble Bee are likely far greater than those of a Big Horn. Kind of makes you wonder what the heck Ford and Chevy are doing leaving the entire segment to Ram. [Stellantis]
🐎 Speaking of muscle cars, we drove the 2026 Ford Mustang RTR and the old-school handbrake is the star of the show. Don’t sneer at its turbo-four powertrain because this Mustang is far more fun than you think. [The Drive]
🚙 As BMW trims its lineup to save costs the automaker’s considering a new SUV that would be larger, and presumably more expensive, than the X7 as a range topper to take on the upcoming Audi Q9. [Motor1]
📉 General Motors, Ford, and Stellantis expect to lose marketshare to the Asian competition as third-quarter sales results filter out, according to analysts, thanks to the Iran war, fuel prices, and buyers seeking fuel-efficient models. [Reuters]
🔨 Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa said the automaker’s tackling its quality woes and has established nearly 50 war rooms staffed by engineers focused on quality. “We are fixing them very, very, very quickly. We have a target to get, in 2028, first quartile in quality with all the segments and markets where we compete, and we will get there,” Filosa said. [Automotive News]
🛂 The 2027 Honda Passport is now arriving at dealers and costs $42,790 including a $1,595 destination charge. [Motor1]
🇳🇱 Longtime BMW tuner AC Schnitzer was set to close after 39 years, but a Dutch company, AM Group, has stepped in and saved the legendary German tuner. [BMWblog]
💎 The Aston Martin DBX GT debuted with a focus on long-distance luxury as a grand tourer. The plusher version of the automaker’s SUV features a twin-turbo V8 under its hood and is said to be “aimed at customers who prefer assured elegance over sporting aggression and demand a higher degree of luxury.” [Autocar]
😍 A Porsche 944 has been transformed into a shooting brake and dubbed the GT-K44. Each one will cost over $132,000 at current exchange rates. [Top Gear]
Got a tip or feedback for The Downshift? Reach out to tips@thedrive.com

source_texts.title: [EMBARGO] Ram’s Entry-Level Rumble Bee Sold Out In 90 Minutes
source_texts.summary: It took less than two hours for the entire 2026 allocation of the Rumble Bee 5.7-liter V8 to be spoken for
source_texts.text:
- Ram filled the 2026 allocation of the entry-level Rumble Bee in 90 minutes.
- Model was sold out through March 2027 within 24 hours, proving strong demand.
- Base Rumble Bee will be followed by 392 and SRT variants next year.
When Ram brought the 5.7-liter Hemi V8 engine back from the dead, customers showed their appreciation by cracking open their wallets and ordering more than 10,000 trucks in 24 hours. The buzz continues and it’s helping to lift the new 1500 Rumble Bee.
Within 90 minutes, the entire 2026 calendar-year allocation of the Rumble Bee with the 5.7-liter V8 was sold out. The buying frenzy didn’t stop there as the order book was filled through March 2027 within 24 hours.
That has to be a huge relief for Ram as the company took a gamble on bringing muscle trucks back. As Tim Kuniskis previously told us, the Rumble Bee wasn’t a “safe bet” as street trucks have never really worked out well in the past.
However, Ram did their homework and made muscle trucks more practical. As part of this effort, the Rumble Bee is quad cab-only and offers an extensive lineup that includes an affordable base model, a mid-level 392 variant, and an extreme SRT version with 777 hp (579 kW / 788 PS).
Given the high demand, Ram said “sold customer orders within the allocation will receive priority status.” The brand noted this should help to ensure customers get their trucks as quickly as possible.
Ram CEO Matt VanDyke remarked, “The speed at which the Rumble Bee sold out speaks volumes about the passion our customers have for performance trucks. By pairing legendary Hemi V8 power with Ram capability and a distinctive design, we’ve delivered a truck that captures the spirit of modern American muscle.”
The entry-level Ram 1500 Rumble Bee starts at $59,995 and has a 5.7-liter Hemi V8 that eschews stop/start and eTorque systems. It produces 395 hp (295 kW / 400 PS) and 410 lb-ft (555 Nm) of torque, and is connected to an eight-speed automatic transmission as well as an active four-wheel drive system. This setup enables the model to accelerate from 0-60 mph (0-96 km/h) in 6.1 seconds and run the quarter mile in 14.6 seconds at 93 mph (150 km/h).
